clue.text: Pointed remark made in pub by bishop

parts.note: a bar is a pub, or the counter in one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric in a pub makes a cutting comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a hurtful or wounding comment, a remark with a sharp point to it.

clue.text: One may hold papers in short legal action

explanation.surface: Documents are kept for a quick court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One may hold papers' is a definition by example, so its question-free form works as a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag for carrying documents, so it is something that holds papers.

clue.text: Complicated procedure pouring millions into capital function

indicators.note: pouring something into a vessel puts it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
M is the abbreviation for millions
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: An elaborate scheme pumps millions into the workings of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tediously complicated process or set of formalities.

clue.text: Was brilliant securing work across America demonstrating a musical instrument

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another
lying across something means spanning it from side to side, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the usual abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A performer dazzles while touring the States, showing off a band instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: OP spans USA to give OUSAP, and SHONE secures that: S-OUSAP-HONE gives SOUSAPHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sousaphone is a large brass tuba variant worn around the body, named after the bandmaster John Philip Sousa.

clue.text: Old leader of Turks greeting Desdemona's husband

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: An elderly Ottoman leader says hello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play, Othello, the Moorish general, marries Desdemona.

clue.text: Predicaments caused by quarrels about Ecstasy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Trouble comes from fights over drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapes are awkward or difficult situations, as in getting into scrapes.

clue.text: More papers translated about end of reign of William and Mary, say

indicators.note: translating changes words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the end is the final position, so only the closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: Extra documents are translated about the close of the reign of the joint monarchs William and Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the royal couple, but the definition treats William and Mary simply as names; 'about' tells you the N joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: William and Mary are examples of proper names, nouns naming particular people and written with a capital.

clue.text: Snow leopard, one of sixteen in a pound

definitions.meaning: first meaning: another name for the snow leopard

definitions.text: one of sixteen in a pound
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a unit of weight, a sixteenth of an imperial pound

explanation.walkthrough: The animal and the weight are unrelated meanings of the same word; 'pound' suggests an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is an old name for the snow leopard, and there are sixteen avoirdupois ounces in a pound weight.

clue.text: Extremely exhilarating conclusion to army exercises in country

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept
a conclusion comes last, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: Army drills end on a thrilling note somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Turn on one, a villainous ensign

indicators.note: placed on in an across clue means written after the preceding pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone rounds on a treacherous junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming ensign, a junior officer rank, who destroys Othello in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Cautious about girl offering wine

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: Donna is a girl's name, and Italian for lady

explanation.surface: A wary approach to a young woman who is handing round drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white grape variety and the dry white table drink made from it.

clue.text: Soft soap used with facecloth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flattering or evasive talk
second meaning: a small cloth for washing the face

explanation.surface: Instructions for washing your face: gentle soap and a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' looks like bathroom kit to go with the cloth, but it is the figurative sense of smooth persuasive talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for evasive smooth talk, and also the British word for a washcloth.

clue.text: Love child eating one, a piece of cake

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beloved child munches a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' and 'piece of cake' make a tidy food picture, but the cake is an idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Gift of pence — consider as an affront

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pence
to resent something is to take it as an insult

explanation.surface: Someone is insulted at being handed a few coppers as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given freely, a synonym for a gift.

clue.text: Many thousands milling about round federation's capital for ages

indicators.note: a crowd milling about moves aimlessly in all directions, so the letters are mixed up
a capital is the letter at the head of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Huge crowds mill around a federal capital for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the anagram signal, but it supplies the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A month of Sundays is an idiom for a very long time, as in 'not in a month of Sundays'.

clue.text: Native of Lincoln checking roots?

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back or restrain it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name

explanation.surface: Someone from Lincoln is investigating their ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city, but it is the US president, Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, a native of it.

clue.text: Observer magazine

definitions.meaning: second meaning: The ..., a British weekly political magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, so the clue looks like two publications; only the second is.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, and The Spectator is a long-running British current-affairs weekly.

clue.text: At home in flat, good girl produces a type of oil

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the letters that follow it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A well-behaved young woman, home in her apartment, makes some kind of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good girl' reads as one phrase, but good is just G and the girl is the name Primrose.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening primrose oil, pressed from the seeds of a yellow-flowered plant, is sold as a dietary supplement.

clue.text: Popular male entertained by girl in seedy bar

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so these pieces go inside another

parts.note: Gill is a girl's name, as in Jack and Gill
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A well-liked man is treated by a young woman in a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin mill is American slang for a cheap, disreputable drinking place.

clue.text: Draws Hornung character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lotteries with prizes drawn from tickets
second meaning: the gentleman thief created by E. W. Hornung

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like a verb about a sketching author, but it is a plural noun for prize draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles are lottery-style prize draws, and A. J. Raffles is Hornung's cricketing burglar hero.

clue.text: The sort of wedding one must be expecting to have?

definitions.text: The sort of wedding one must be expecting to have?

parts.words: The sort of wedding one must be expecting to have?
parts.note: surface reading: the kind of wedding a couple anticipates and plans for
setter's reading: expecting means pregnant, so this is a wedding hurried along because a baby is on the way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like anticipation, but it means pregnant: the wedding is one forced on the couple, traditionally at the point of the bride's father's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun wedding is a hasty marriage arranged because the bride is pregnant.

clue.text: Female with a fiver, initially produced from bundle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A woman pulls a five-pound note from a wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiver is a five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, of corn stalks or of papers tied together.

clue.text: Willow, very large one approaching outskirts of Esher

indicators.note: approaching means coming up next to, so the pieces sit side by side in sequence

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: A huge willow tree stands near the edge of Esher.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Neo-Nazi fellow is cast out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A far-right man gets expelled from a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast out' reads as one phrase meaning expelled, but cast is part of the letters and out the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi holds extreme far-right authoritarian views, so is a modern fascist.

clue.text: Real idiots misread leading articles

indicators.note: something misread is taken in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine fools have misunderstood the newspaper's opinion pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article, or leader, is a newspaper's editorial stating the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: One put in large order

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone places a bulk order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large order' reads as a big purchase, but order is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command, an order issued by someone in power.

clue.text: In which one starting school may be excellent

definitions.text: In which one starting school may be
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the first form a child is put in
second meaning: of the very highest quality

explanation.surface: A new pupil may turn out to be outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as the start of a sentence about a pupil, but it is a whimsical definition of the class a beginner joins.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class means top-quality, and literally the first class at school is where a new child begins.

clue.text: Couple on the radio promoting fruit

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Two presenters advertise fruit on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet, juicy tree fruit, an example of the category.
